bull_bear.body:
- Management states the BOPP Film Line at Jammu has a substantial competitive advantage, positioning it favourably for long-term growth and profitability
- Established, successfully operating BOPET plant at Panagarh serving Indian demand with a special focus on Eastern India
- Proven export channel: DPFPL has started exporting its product successfully in many parts of the world including neighbouring countries, and intends to keep growing exports
- New BOPET capacity is a brownfield expansion on existing land adjacent to the operational facility, with the advance to machinery supplier Brückner Maschinenbau GmbH already paid
- Stable promoter/holding structure: Dhunseri Investments Ltd. holds 65.23% of equity share capital as on March 31, 2026
- Internal control system reviewed through Internal Audit and monitored regularly by the Executive Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer, with escalation to the Audit Committee and Board
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macro dependence — business strategy tied to the country's economic environment — The MD&A states the business strategy is largely dependent on the economic environment of the country and that any slowdown of economic growth could adversely affect the Company's performance, leaving earnings exposed to a cycle the Company does not control.
- Financial-market volatility on the treasury book — With one of only two segments being 'Treasury Operations' in shares and securities of other bodies corporate, volatility in the financial market could adversely affect performance; management attributes the year's weaker ratios to lower contribution from investment-related income streams and negative returns on disposal of financial assets.
- Narrow, non-operating earnings base — Income comprised mainly revenue from trading activities, investments, royalty and dividend from Joint Ventures across just two segments ('Treasury Operations' and 'Trading activities'), so earnings quality depends on income streams outside a core manufacturing operation.
- Investment / subsidiary impairment risk — The Company wrote off its investment in subsidiary Twelve Cupcakes Pte. Ltd., Singapore pursuant to its liquidation process, a one-time exceptional write-off of a foreign subsidiary that management cites as a driver of the decline in returns.
- Government policy change — Management continues to review the business strategy from time to time depending on changes in Government policies, indicating policy shifts can force strategy resets.
- Project execution and geo-political disruption — The subsidiary's Jammu project saw temporary disruption of activities due to the geo-political situation before restarting, showing commissioning timelines for the BOPP lines are exposed to events outside management control.
- Challenging film-industry market conditions — Management describes it as a challenging business that may take some time to witness a significant improvement in market conditions, which delays the payback on the group's film capacity.
- Industry downturn and regulatory/litigation environment (cautionary statement) — The MD&A cautionary statement flags a downtrend in the industry, global or domestic or both, significant changes in the political and economic environment in India, applicable statutes and litigation as developments that could affect operations.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company carries on the business of treasury operations in shares and securities of other bodies corporate and commodity trading including trading of PET Resins, and reports under two segments, "Treasury Operations" and "Trading activities". Its income during the year under review comprised mainly income/revenue from trading activities, investments, royalty and dividend from Joint Ventures, and total employee strength as on March 31, 2026 stood at 18. Dhunseri Investments Ltd. continues to be the Holding Company holding 65.23% of the equity share capital as on March 31, 2026, while wholly-owned subsidiaries Dhunseri Poly Films Pvt. Ltd. (BOPET/BOPP films) and Dhunseri Infrastructure Ltd. (Dhunseri Commercial Park) hold the group's operating and development assets.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Run the Company as a treasury and trading platform: treasury operations in shares and securities of other bodies corporate plus commodity trading including trading of PET Resins, with the business strategy reviewed from time to time depending on changes in Government policies.
- Grow exports of BOPET film through wholly-owned subsidiary Dhunseri Poly Films Pvt. Ltd. (DPFPL), which has started exporting successfully to many parts of the world including neighbouring countries and focuses to continue growing exports.
- Serve Indian BOPET demand with a special focus on Eastern India from the operating Panagarh, West Bengal plant.
- Complete DPFPL's Jammu BOPP project in two lines, positioning the Jammu BOPP Film Line as a substantial competitive advantage for long-term growth and profitability.
- Expand BOPET capacity via a brownfield New Line Project at Panagarh Industrial Park adjacent to the existing operational facility on existing land.
- The Board of Directors has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy as required by Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, which is published on the Company's website. Governance of capital and risk rests with Board committees: the Risk Management Committee (Mr. R.K.Sharma as Chairperson, with Prof. A.K.Dutta and Mr. B.Bajoria as Members) operates under a Board-approved Risk Management Policy whose major mechanisms are monitoring of statutory, legal and investment compliances and internal audit, while the Audit Committee comprises the Executive Chairman, four Non-Executive Independent Directors and one Non-Executive & Non-Independent Director and oversees financial reporting and related party disclosures. The Company states it has adequate internal financial controls under Section 134(5)(e), tested during the year with no material weakness observed in design or operation. The sections provided do not set out a quantified payout, buyback or leverage philosophy beyond the policy itself.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is concentrated in the wholly-owned subsidiary Dhunseri Poly Films Pvt. Ltd. (DPFPL) rather than at the standalone level. DPFPL's BOPET manufacturing plant at Panagarh, West Bengal is operating successfully, catering to demand in India with special focus on Eastern India and export. As part of its expansion plan, DPFPL is setting up a brownfield BOPET New Line Project at Panagarh Industrial Park, West Bengal with installed capacity of 59,200 TPA, adjacent to its existing 52,000 MTPA operational BOPET facility on the existing land; the new line is expected to commence commercial production in April 2028 and the advance to machinery supplier Brückner Maschinenbau GmbH has already been paid. Separately, DPFPL's project in Jammu is progressing largely as per plan after a temporary disruption of activities due to the geo-political situation; management is targeting to start operation of the first BOPP production line tentatively from August/September 2026, with the second line expected to start from the first quarter of 2027, and states the Jammu BOPP Film Line has a substantial competitive advantage positioning it favourably for long-term growth and profitability. In the other wholly-owned subsidiary, Dhunseri Infrastructure Ltd., development of an IT Complex on leasehold land admeasuring 3.03 acres inside a Special Economic Zone has remained constrained owing to adverse conditions and other external factors; the project has been renamed "Dhunseri Commercial Park" following the reclassification of SEZs as Multi-Sector Special Economic Zones, and the Group is actively evaluating alternatives for optimal utilisation of the developed space including possible de-notification for broader commercial use.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Business strategy is largely dependent on the economic environment of the country; any slowdown of economic growth or volatility in the financial market could adversely affect the Company's performance.
- Management sees Government of India's efforts on economic growth, startups and infrastructure development as creating opportunities the Company is looking to tap at the right moment.
- Film business remains challenging: management states it may take some time to witness a significant improvement in market conditions.
- The Panagarh BOPET plant is operating successfully and catering to demand in India with a special focus on Eastern India and export, with exports already established in many parts of the world including neighbouring countries.
- The Jammu project saw temporary disruption of activities due to the geo-political situation, but activities have restarted and the project is progressing largely as per plan.
- Earnings mix is exposed to investment-related income streams and disposals of financial assets, which management cites as the reason for weaker ratios during the year.
- One-time exceptional write-off relating to a foreign subsidiary (Twelve Cupcakes Pte. Ltd., Singapore, in liquidation) weighed on the year's outcome.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Dhunseri Ventures Limited is a promoter-controlled investment and trading company running treasury operations in shares and securities alongside commodity trading of PET Resins, with the group's manufacturing (BOPET/BOPP packaging films) and property assets held through wholly-owned subsidiaries.

open.item: DPFPL is targeting to start operation of the first BOPP production line at its Jammu project tentatively from August/September 2026.
Directors have recommended a dividend of Rs.1.50 per equity share of Rs.10 each for the year ended March 31, 2026, subject to shareholders' approval at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.
The second BOPP line at DPFPL's Jammu project is expected to start operation from the first quarter of 2027.

DPFPL is setting up a brownfield BOPET New Line Project at Panagarh Industrial Park, West Bengal with installed capacity of 59,200 TPA adjacent to its existing 52,000 MTPA facility, expected to commence commercial production in April 2028.

The Group is actively evaluating alternatives for optimal utilisation of the developed space at Dhunseri Commercial Park, including possible de-notification of the area under SEZ regulations for broader commercial and other permissible purposes.
DPFPL intends to continue growing its exports of BOPET film in the future.
